research_rationale:
Executive Order 9938 (13 FR 1555 (Federal Register of March 24, 1948)) revokes Executive Order No. 9544 of April 25, 1945, which had authorized and directed the Secretary of War to assume full control of a public airport in Oregon on described lands (T. 15 S., R. 13 E., Willamette Meridian, 1,520 acres). The held Federal Register text prints the heading of Executive Order 9938 and its paragraphs up to the words “it is intended that the lease shall again be operative and”, where the page breaks (the page notes that the order continues on a later page); the closing words and the signing line are not in the held Federal Register bytes. The American Presidency Project mirror text for the same order is complete and ends with the signing line of March 22, 1948; it is not cited as a source in this claim, because an official copy is held, but it agrees with the Federal Register text up to the break and gives the signing date as March 22, 1948, the date in the register. The operative command is the revocation of Executive Order No. 9544, which the order says “is hereby revoked”. The order also says the lands are included in a twenty-year lease to the City of Redmond that began March 12, 1942, and states the intention that the lease again be operative. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: the order states no effective date in the held bytes, so it took effect when it was signed on March 22, 1948, and the revocation was exhausted by performance on that date. The machine own-term candidate of 1962-03-12 is the end of the Redmond lease described in the order; it is a fact about the lease and not an end of the order's revocation, so it is not used. A search of the held texts for the order's number found no later order citing it. The Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9544 stays revoked and the lease operates again; that consequence is not a command left to end.
